findings.claim: The new setAutoCommit(true) rule also fires when the call sits after the last executeUpdate but before conn.commit(), with the message 'turns auto-commit back on before the transfer is committed, so each update is saved on its own'. For that placement this is technically wrong: per the Connection.setAutoCommit NOTE, switching auto-commit on during a transaction commits the open transaction, so both already-successful updates are committed together, and the following conn.commit() then fails in pgJDBC with 'Cannot commit when autoCommit is enabled.' Rejecting the code is right; the stated reason is not.
findings.recommendation: Split the message by position: before the last executeUpdate keep 'each update is saved on its own'; between the last update and commit() say 'turning auto-commit on here commits the transaction early, and conn.commit() then throws because auto-commit is on. Restore it only after commit() and rollback(), for example in a finally block.'

items.note: Resolved. Ran the extracted t3Check in node: the correct transfer passes with and without finally { conn.setAutoCommit(true); } after the catch (Oracle Using Transactions pattern); setAutoCommit(true) before the updates, between them, or before commit() is rejected; missing setAutoCommit(false) and early commit() are still rejected. The old blanket 'true keeps auto-commit on' message is gone. The wording for the before-commit() placement is imprecise; raised separately as new low finding tx-sme-r-001.
